answer: A nebula mesh admits only agents that stake 3,000 POA at a vertex node and pass a ripple test before trading. Each newcomer needs five established neighbours as sponsors, who lose 2,000 POA if their guest cheats, and a ripple of its ten trades is published on-chain for all to audit. Stakes stay locked for three epochs, and stewards revoke any vertex that vouches twice from one machine. Faking one trusted trader needs 25 vertices, 75,000 POA staked and 125 sponsor bonds — a cost no bot farm can afford. Like a nebula held together by stars, trust forms only where the light is genuine.
